figures.finding: Hungary refunds 30% of the direct production costs spent in the country to cinema and television films, through companies that receive tax relief for supporting them via the National Film Institute's Collection Account; adding non-Hungarian costs up to 7.5% raises the base to 37.5%; the scheme is secured to the end of 2030 and the annual amount on the Collection Account for 2026 is HUF 70 billion; principal photography must start within six months of registration.

value.base: direct film production costs spent in Hungary
value.form: cash refund (post-financing) via sponsor companies' tax relief, guaranteed through the NFI Collection Account

figures.applies: Hungary; domestic and international productions registered with the National Film Office; 2026.

sources.said: Films (for cinema and television) produced in Hungary are eligible for a 30% rebate based on their expenditure (all the direct film production costs) spent in the country. … The 30% incentive is extendable to 37.5% of the eligible production expense by adding 7.5% non-Hungarian costs. (The non-Hungarian eligible spend is capped at 25% of the rebate.) … has been secured until the end of 2030. … the annual Film Incentive available on the collection account for supporting film productions will be HUF 70 billion in 2026. Furthermore, principal photography must be started within six months of receiving the decision on registration for support
